subject: Renewal Annex: Dedicated pool tokens/sec assurance & SLA fallback — Datashift
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@datashift.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — proposal for Dedicated expansion + tokens/sec annex

Hi Sarah,

Following our renewal planning call last week, attached is a concise annex that captures the dedicated pool expansion we discussed and the tokens/sec (throughput) assurances Datashift needs for the new feature rollout in Q4. High level: you asked for an additional 16 GPUs in a reserved pool, a committed tokens/sec baseline for critical endpoints, and a fallback policy that preserves availability while protecting other tenants.

Attached: Datashift_TokensPS_Addendum_v2.pdf (draft annex) and a short XLS with projected token consumption under the proposed commit.

Quick summary in case helpful:
- Reserved pool: +16 A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated)
- Committed throughput: 60k tokens/sec sustained (90th percentile) across three production endpoints
- Burst window: up to 120k tokens/sec for 30s, subject to onboarded burst credits
- Fallback & routing: automatic fallback to compatible quantized model variant at 95th percentile overage; cross-region spillover permitted (same-account region)
- Credits: service credit schedule in annex tied to sustained breach beyond consecutive 10-minute windows

Key asks from us to get this executed: confirmation on the committed tokens/sec numbers, preferred legal owner for the annex (procurement vs legal), and whether you want us to include a stricter penalty ladder or a simple credit schedule.

If useful, I can loop Ben from Legal and Neha from Customer Success into the next thread to lock language. Are you available Wed 12th or Thu 13th for a 30-minute alignment?

Thanks — I’ll stand up a DocuSign draft once we lock numbers.

Best,
Jonas

Subject: Re: Renewal planning — proposal for Dedicated expansion + tokens/sec annex

Jonas — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple clarifying points from product/procurement:

1) Committed throughput: our initial analysis expects ~48–55k tokens/sec sustained per peak microservice, but we want to budget headroom. Would you consider 65k tokens/sec as the committed baseline and keep the 120k burst?

2) Burst credit mechanics: Tom asked how credits are consumed and replenished (monthly bucket vs rolling). Can you call that out in the annex?

3) Fallback behavior: engineering insists on a deterministic fallback ordering (primary quantized variant, then region spill to our secondary region). We need the annex to enumerate that flow and expected latency delta when fallback is active.

4) Legal: procurement wants the credit schedule visible in the body of the annex rather than buried in an appendix.

We can do Wed 12th 4pm PT or Thu 13th 9am PT to finalize. Procurement prefers a quick 20–30m to sign off if the numbers hold.

—Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Platform — Datashift
[sarah.kim@datashift.ai]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@datashift.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — proposal for Dedicated expansion + tokens/sec annex

Sarah — great questions, and yes we can accommodate the changes you requested. Summary of adjustments we propose (I’ve also updated the draft annex attached):

- Committed throughput: set to 65,000 tokens/sec (sustained target measured as 90th percentile over rolling 30-day windows) across the named production endpoints.
- Burst model: 120,000 tokens/sec for up to 30s per burst event; bursts consume burst credits drawn from a monthly pool (default replenishment on the 1st of each month). Unused burst credits roll over for one month.
- Fallback/order: 1) quantized-compatible model variant in-region (expected latency +40–80ms); 2) cross-region spill to DR region (expected latency +200–400ms); 3) best-effort degraded mode (token throttling) if both fail. Annex has a sequence diagram and latency deltas.
- Credit schedule: included in body — credits accrue as a percentage of monthly invoice based on minutes of sustained breach per 10-minute window. Example table in annex (see pages 2–3).

I’ve attached the revised PDF (Datashift_TokensPS_Addendum_v2.pdf) with the above language marked and a short runbook section for ops. Laura — adding you here to confirm the latency deltas and fallbacks are accurate to our runtime behavior; can you scan page 5?

If that all looks good I’ll ask Ben to prep the legal wording and then prepare a DocuSign powerform for signature. I can do Thu 13th 9am PT for the quick review.

Cheers,
Jonas

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Jul 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft legal language for Datashift tokens/sec annex

Hi Sarah / procurement,

I reviewed the proposed operational terms and drafted a concise legal annex that preserves the commercial intent and keeps the credit mechanics simple to automate. Key legal points (excerpt):

- "Committed Throughput" means the aggregate tokens-per-second commitment set forth in Annex A, measured at the Redwood ingress gateway prior to any throttling or fallback. Sustained breach is measured as 90th percentile over a rolling 30-day period.
- Service Credits: If Sustained Breach occurs for more than three (3) non-overlapping 10-minute windows in a calendar month, Datashift shall be eligible for service credits equal to 2% of the monthly Dedicated subscription fee per additional 10-minute window, capped at 30% for the month. Credits will be applied to the subsequent invoice.
- Burst Credits & Replenishment: Burst credits are consumed lexicographically by event; unused burst credits roll over for one month.
- Fallback & Mitigation: Redwood will first attempt in-region quantized variant (expected delta +40–80ms). If capacity not available, Redwood may route requests to a secondary region for which Datashift grants temporary cross-region processing.

I attached the legal annex as a Word document for your redlines. If procurement needs different credit thresholds we can iterate quickly. Once redlines are stable I will finalize the DocuSign envelope.

Ben Carter
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
[ben.carter@redwood.com]

Ben / Jonas — thank you. Procurement reviewed the Word draft and we’ve got two small asks before we route for signature: (1) raise the first credit threshold to 4 non-overlapping 10-minute windows before credits apply; (2) call out an exception window for scheduled maintenance (we’ll allow a 60-minute monthly maintenance window to be exempted provided Redwood gives 72 hours’ notice).

Assuming those two edits are included we’re ready to sign this week. Please send the DocuSign link when ready.

Thanks — Sarah
